name: Dana Incorporated

profile.description: Dana Incorporated supplies power-conveyance and energy-management systems -- driveline, e-propulsion, and thermal-management components -- for on-highway light, commercial, and off-highway vehicles across North America, Europe, South America, and Asia Pacific [1]. R. Bruce McDonald, former Chairman and CEO of Adient, took over as Chairman and CEO in November 2024 following James Kamsickas's retirement, and immediately pursued a strategic reshaping of the company, completing the sale of the Off-Highway business at a $2.7 billion enterprise value to focus on a streamlined, higher-margin on-highway and e-propulsion portfolio [2]. Dana reported approximately $7.5 billion in 2025 sales with adjusted EBITDA of roughly $600 million (8% margin), used Off-Highway sale proceeds to cut debt by $1.9 billion, and has set a 'Dana 2030' target of ~$10 billion in sales at 14-15% adjusted EBITDA margins [1].

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): New CEO McDonald executed a major portfolio reshaping within his first year -- divesting the Off-Highway segment for $2.7B and using proceeds to cut debt by $1.9B -- while the prior nine-year CEO tenure grew sales 80% and built what is described as a 'high-performance culture' [2]. AI Deployment (0/2): No specific AI-driven product, manufacturing, or design initiative was identified in company disclosures or press coverage. Market Share (1/2): Dana holds a top-tier global position in driveline and e-propulsion systems for light and commercial vehicles, evidenced by new OEM platform wins, though it competes closely with BorgWarner, American Axle, and Magna without outright category dominance [1]. Pipeline (2/2): A three-year new-business backlog grew from $750 million to $950 million by Q1 2026, driven by next-generation platform awards including the RAM Dakota program (an estimated $250 million in annual sales starting 2028), providing multi-year revenue visibility [1][2]. R&D Intensity (1/1): McDonald has stated Dana is 'differentiated by leading technology innovation,' with continued engineering investment in e-propulsion systems even as the $200 million cost-reduction program reflects slower-than-expected EV adoption [2].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Dana's stated purpose -- improving 'the efficiency, performance, and sustainability of powered vehicles and machinery' -- ties concretely to the broader energy-transition narrative, though it is not deeply distinctive versus peers like BorgWarner pursuing similar electrification positioning [1][2]. Community Impact (1/2): The company maintains a dedicated sustainability report, board-level sustainability oversight, and supply-chain sustainability programs, representing standard-practice ESG infrastructure rather than a distinctive community program [3]. Employee Retention (0/2): While the prior CEO's tenure is credited with building a 'high-performance culture,' the concurrent $200 million cost-reduction program and 2024 leadership transition create near-term restructuring risk that works against retention strength. Insider Buying (0/2): No evidence of meaningful net insider purchases was identified in the research period.

infrastructure.label: DEVELOPING
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on available metrics as a Growth stock. Dana clears the liquidity floor comfortably with ~1.59 million average daily shares at $29.96 (~$47.6M daily turnover) [4]. D/E of 75.8% is close to the 70% target, and forward P/E of 7.16 is well inside the 20x target, reflecting a depressed valuation relative to the 2026 EBITDA-margin recovery plan. Profit margin of 14.55% trails the 20% target but is respectable given the recent divestiture-driven transition, and revenue growth YoY of 3.9% (continuing operations) is roughly at the midpoint of the target range. The two biggest drags (both 2x weighted) are ROE of -1.63%, scored at the floor given negative profitability on a trailing basis, and PEG of 4.21, far above the 3.0 floor, reflecting that current earnings estimates do not yet capture the anticipated 2026-2030 margin expansion. Revenue growth 5-year CAGR is not meaningful given the Off-Highway divestiture materially distorts historical top-line comparability and is therefore excluded rather than mechanically penalized.

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (7/9): Dana's business -- physical driveline, axle, and e-propulsion hardware bolted into vehicles -- cannot be replaced by AI software, and the shift toward electrification and eventual autonomy is more likely to increase content-per-vehicle (thermal management, e-propulsion systems) than displace it [1][2]. Regulatory and OEM qualification requirements further protect incumbent suppliers like Dana from new-entrant disruption. AI Opportunity (0/1): No disclosed AI-specific product or revenue stream was identified; the company's technology narrative centers on electrification and engineering content rather than AI-driven software products.

infinite_game.summary: Dana has undertaken a genuinely existential strategic pivot -- selling its historic Off-Highway business to reposition as a focused, higher-margin on-highway and e-propulsion supplier -- while balancing a still-nascent EV transition against near-term cost discipline. The new CEO's early moves demonstrate real courage and adaptability, but a recent leadership change and an associated cost-reduction program (implying layoffs) leave open questions about organizational trust during the transition.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): Dana's mission to improve the 'efficiency, performance, and sustainability of powered vehicles and machinery' connects concretely to the broader energy transition and is reinforced by continued e-propulsion R&D investment even amid a cost-reduction program, though it remains a supplier-level cause shared with several competitors rather than a category-defining one [1][2].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): The prior nine-year CEO built what is described as a 'high-performance culture' that drove 80% sales growth, but the November 2024 CEO transition and the concurrent $200 million cost-reduction program (implying workforce reductions) create near-term uncertainty about whether that culture persists under new leadership [2].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (1/1 partial): Dana competes with BorgWarner, American Axle, and Magna for OEM platform sourcing largely on engineering merit -- evidenced by the competitively won RAM Dakota program -- rather than predatory pricing or exclusionary tactics [1][2].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (2/2): Selling the Off-Highway business -- long a core, historically identity-defining segment -- for $2.7 billion to deleverage and refocus on higher-margin on-highway/e-propulsion products is precisely the kind of dramatic, identity-level reinvention Sinek associates with existential flexibility, undertaken within McDonald's first year as CEO [2].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (2/2): Divesting a major, revenue-generating legacy segment and accepting a near-term ~$2.6 billion revenue decline (from $10.16B in 2022 to $7.5B in 2025) in exchange for a cleaner, more focused, deleveraged platform represents a genuinely costly strategic sacrifice for longer-term positioning [1][2].

investment_thesis: Dana has repositioned itself in under a year under new CEO Bruce McDonald, selling the Off-Highway business for $2.7 billion, cutting debt by $1.9 billion, and refocusing on a higher-margin on-highway and e-propulsion platform with a 2026 EBITDA-margin target of 10-11% en route to a 'Dana 2030' goal of ~$10 billion in sales at 14-15% margins [1][2]. A growing three-year new-business backlog ($750M to $950M by Q1 2026), anchored by the newly won RAM Dakota program, provides real multi-year revenue visibility, and the stock's 7.16x forward P/E prices in substantial skepticism relative to management's own margin-expansion roadmap. A strong Inspire Insight score of 69 (ALIGNED), spanning sixteen positive attributions including Employee Wellbeing, Ethical Labor Practices, and Environmental Risk Mitigation, reflects genuinely robust ESG practices for an industrial supplier.
thesis_continued: The bear case centers on unproven execution and weak current profitability: trailing ROE is negative (-1.63%), PEG of 4.21 is far above a reasonable growth-adjusted valuation, and the $200 million cost-reduction program explicitly acknowledges that EV adoption has been slower than the company originally underwrote, undercutting part of the electrification thesis [2]. Revenue has fallen from $10.16 billion in 2022 to $7.5 billion in 2025, a decline driven primarily by the Off-Highway divestiture but nonetheless reducing the scale over which fixed costs are spread during the transition. D/E of 75.8% remains modestly above the 70% target despite the recent $1.9 billion debt paydown, leaving limited room for missteps if the margin-expansion plan slips. This is a plausible self-help turnaround story, but it remains early and unproven against a 2030 target still four years away [1][2].
key_catalysts: Continued progress on the $325 million cost-reduction program and 2026 EBITDA margin target of 10-11% would validate the post-divestiture operating model and could re-rate the stock off its current 7.16x forward P/E [1]

Ramp of the RAM Dakota program (targeted at $250 million in annual sales starting 2028) and further new-business wins could extend the backlog beyond the current $950 million three-year figure, reinforcing revenue visibility [1][2]

Further debt reduction using the remaining Off-Highway sale proceeds could bring D/E meaningfully below the 70% target, improving the balance-sheet risk profile ahead of the 'Dana 2030' targets [1][2]
key_risks: A further slowdown in EV/e-propulsion adoption beyond what is already reflected in the $200 million cost-reduction program could delay the path to the 2026 EBITDA-margin target and the longer-term 'Dana 2030' goals [2]

Trailing return on equity of -1.63% and a PEG of 4.21 indicate the market has not yet been shown proof that the post-divestiture, more focused Dana can generate returns commensurate with its growth targets [4]
The concurrent CEO transition and cost-reduction (workforce) program create execution and culture-continuity risk at a critical moment in the company's strategic repositioning [2]

backlog.note: Dana does not publish a traditional book-to-bill ratio; the figures here reflect the company's disclosed 3-year new-business backlog from awarded next-generation OEM light- and commercial-vehicle platforms, which grew from $750 million to $950 million between the 2025 year-end update and Q1 2026, driven by the RAM Dakota program win (~$250 million in annual sales starting 2028). These are firm sourcing awards for future platform launches rather than a queue of unfulfilled near-term orders, so book-to-bill and backlog-to-revenue-quarter metrics used for defense/industrial peers are not directly comparable here.
